## Validation and sources

### Domain recovery

1. `GET /repos/octomation/vanity/pages` initially returned `cname: null`.
2. After the user's verification, `PUT /repos/octomation/vanity/pages` with
   `cname=go.octolab.org` succeeded. GitHub returned
   `protected_domain_state: verified` and issued a certificate.
3. `PUT /repos/octomation/vanity/pages` with `https_enforced=true` succeeded.
   A subsequent GET returned `cname: go.octolab.org`, `https_enforced: true`,
   `html_url: https://go.octolab.org/`, and certificate state `approved`.
4. Normal TLS verification with curl and Python's default SSL context passed.
   The served certificate is issued by Let's Encrypt YR2, covers
   `go.octolab.org`, and expires on 2026-12-18 at 03:26:19 UTC.
5. HTTPS returned HTTP 200. All three required discovery endpoints passed:
   `/` points to `https://github.com/octolab/pkg`, `/toolkit/cli` to
   `https://github.com/octolab/cli`, and `/toolkit/config` to
   `https://github.com/octolab/config`. The old Pages artifact serves them;
   local recovery changes have not been deployed.
6. HTTP `/toolkit/config` returned 301 to HTTPS. The root HTTP page temporarily
   continued returning the earlier cached 200 response despite enforcement
   being enabled; its response advertises a 600-second cache lifetime.

### Direct module downloads

`make check` (`bin/lib/core/check.bash:1`) first confirmed all three HTTPS
metadata endpoints. Unmodified network attempts then hit a local IPv6 socket
error reaching `sum.golang.org`, separate from vanity discovery. TLS was not
disabled, and the checksum database was not bypassed.

To isolate that local networking problem, the same module downloads were run
through a temporary loopback HTTP CONNECT tunnel that connects upstream using
IPv4. It only forwards encrypted TCP streams, does not terminate TLS, and does
not cache or serve modules. `GOPROXY=direct` and `GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org` remained
set. Each Go version received its own initially empty module cache, with
`GOWORK=off`, `GOENV=off`, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, empty `GOFLAGS`, and empty
`GOINSECURE`, `GOPRIVATE`, `GONOPROXY`, and `GONOSUMDB`.

The command under test was:

```sh
go mod download -json \
  go.octolab.org@v0.12.0 \
  go.octolab.org@v0.12.2 \
  go.octolab.org/toolkit/cli@v0.6.3 \
  go.octolab.org/toolkit/config@v0.0.4
```

Both Go 1.27.1 and Go 1.26.8 produced the same results:

| Module version | Go 1.27.1 | Go 1.26.8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `go.octolab.org@v0.12.0` | Downloaded, checksum verified | Downloaded, checksum verified |
| `go.octolab.org@v0.12.2` | Downloaded, checksum verified | Downloaded, checksum verified |
| `go.octolab.org/toolkit/cli@v0.6.3` | Downloaded, checksum verified | Downloaded, checksum verified |
| `go.octolab.org/toolkit/config@v0.0.4` | `unknown revision v0.0.4` | `unknown revision v0.0.4` |

The successful module and go.mod checksums matched between toolchains. Both
commands returned exit 1 solely because the fourth version is unavailable.

### Missing historical config release

- `GET /repos/octolab/config/tags` and
  `GET /repos/octolab/config/git/matching-refs/tags` both returned only `v0.0.5`.
- Indexit's current `go.mod`, read through the GitHub contents API, explicitly
  requires `go.octolab.org/toolkit/config v0.0.4`.
- The Go proxy still serves `v0.0.4.info`, dated `2020-07-24T19:45:35Z`, and
  the version archive containing 18 files. Its `go.mod` declares Go 1.11,
  `github.com/stretchr/testify v1.6.1`, and `gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.3.0`.
- Comparing the archived files with all 16 commits reachable in the local
  config checkout found no exact match. The original release commit has not
  been identified; no historical tag was reconstructed or reassigned.
- The checksum database has record 1450895 for this immutable version:
  `h1:Q/MnSuRf4ttHCuAaq7PqpD8xQhEtmfK8mO9NX1IxvlA=` for the module and
  `h1:dI3TlD3b4t0ilP7T+q0BYs6mhYBXm8i4TCLqCabykBA=` for `go.mod`.

### User-directed dependency upgrade

After the missing historical release was identified, the user explicitly chose
to upgrade both dependencies. In the indexit working tree, `go.mod:13` now
requires `go.octolab.org/toolkit/cli v0.6.4` and `go.mod:14` requires
`go.octolab.org/toolkit/config v0.0.5`. These are the latest available tags.
CLI v0.6.4 itself requires config v0.0.5, removing the old requirement from
this dependency chain.

- CLI's tagged Go source files are unchanged between v0.6.3 and v0.6.4. The
  config archive's `feature.go`, `secret.go`, and `http/server.go` match v0.0.5.
- `go get` and `go mod tidy` updated four indirect dependencies (Viper, Afero,
  properties, and INI) and added the TOML v2 and YAML v3 dependencies required
  by the updated graph. Other direct dependency versions did not change.
- `go test -mod=readonly -race -timeout=2m ./...` passed on **Go 1.27.1 and
  Go 1.26.8** for the complete indexit package set.
- `go build -mod=readonly -p 2` succeeded on Go 1.27.1; the resulting binary's
  `--help` command succeeded. Its embedded module metadata confirms CLI
  v0.6.4 and config v0.0.5.
- The vanity check now targets CLI v0.6.4 and config v0.0.5
  (`bin/lib/core/check.bash:16`). `make check` passed on **both Go versions**:
  all three HTTPS metadata endpoints passed, and all four module versions
  downloaded directly into fresh temporary caches with checksum verification.
  The IPv4 CONNECT transport described above was used for the local network.
- Successful checks also exposed a cleanup problem: Go's extracted module
  directories are read-only. The check now cleans its private temporary cache
  using `go clean -modcache` (`bin/lib/core/check.bash:10`); both successful
  runs verified that their temporary caches were removed.
- `git diff --check` passed in both repositories. The indexit working tree
  contains changes only to `go.mod` and `go.sum`; no application source changes
  were needed.

The historical config v0.0.4 tag remains absent. The prepared indexit upgrade
no longer depends on it. This supersedes the original requirement to recover
that exact version for indexit; other consumers pinned to it are unaffected.
